title: Quorum Project Config
description: Configuration file for a Quorum project. Place this file at configs/<group_id>.json in your S3 bucket. Quorum uses it to scope the knowledge graph, enforce governance, and identify team members.

group_id.description: Canonical identifier for this project. Must be unique across your Quorum stack. Used as: (1) S3 key prefix — s3://<bucket>/<group_id>/config.json, (2) DynamoDB primary key in quorum-configs and quorum-user-projects, (3) JWT 'project' claim that scopes all graph and audit operations, (4) Graphiti group_id that namespaces the knowledge graph. Must match the filename: configs/<group_id>.json. Lowercase letters, numbers, and hyphens only — no spaces.

project.description: Human-readable display name shown in the dashboard project picker. Optional — falls back to group_id if not set. Unlike group_id, this may contain spaces and mixed case. Never used as a lookup key.

members.description: Team roster. Each member needs at least one identity signal (github_username or git_email) so Quorum can attribute knowledge nodes and compute authority weights.

roles.description: Role definitions that control base_confidence floors. Every role name used in 'members[].role' must appear here. Roles not listed default to base_confidence 0.5.

domains.description: Per-domain governance overrides. Domains segment your knowledge graph by area of concern (e.g. 'auth', 'infra', 'payments'). Each domain can tighten the conflict threshold and restrict which teams may review knowledge in that domain. Domains not listed here inherit the global thresholds.

thresholds.description: Global governance thresholds. Domain-level conflict_threshold overrides take precedence over this global value.

notifications.description: Webhook notification config (GAP-17). When a conflict lands in the human review queue, Quorum POSTs a structured JSON payload to webhook_url. Wire it to Slack, an email relay, or PagerDuty.

guest_access.description: When true, any GitHub-authenticated user can browse this project's knowledge graph in read-only guest mode. Guests have role: null — they see the dashboard but all writes are forced to DRAFT and they have no authority weight.

Member.title: Team Member
Member.description: A single team member record. Maps identity signals to a role so Quorum can attribute knowledge nodes to real people and compute authority weights.

name.description: Display name shown in the dashboard audit trail and conflict resolution UI.

team.description: Team or squad this member belongs to. Used for domain-level required_reviewer_teams checks — a reviewer satisfies the requirement when their team is in the domain's required_reviewer_teams list.

role.description: The member's role key. Must match a key in the top-level 'roles' map. Controls the base_confidence floor applied to this member's knowledge contributions.

github_username.description: GitHub username (case-sensitive). Primary identity signal when QUORUM_GITHUB_TOKEN is configured — used to verify the user's GitHub identity at login. Must exactly match the login returned by GET https://api.github.com/user.

git_email.description: Git committer email. Used as a fallback identity signal when GitHub verification is unavailable, and as the author identity on MCP-originated knowledge nodes.

Role.title: Role Definition
Role.description: Defines the base_confidence floor for a role. Author-provided confidence below this floor is raised to the floor value before the node is written to the graph.

base_confidence.description: Confidence floor for this role (0–1). A principal_architect's writes are inherently more authoritative than a junior's — set this to reflect your team's trust hierarchy. Typical values: 0.90 (principal), 0.80 (senior), 0.70 (engineer), 0.60 (junior).

DomainConfig.title: Domain Config
DomainConfig.description: Per-domain governance overrides. Use stricter conflict_threshold values for sensitive domains (auth, payments, infra) where conflicting knowledge is more dangerous.

conflict_threshold.description: Semantic similarity threshold above which two knowledge nodes in this domain are flagged as potentially conflicting (0–1). Overrides the global thresholds.conflict_threshold for this domain only. Use higher values (0.88–0.95) for sensitive domains to catch near-duplicates that might represent contradictory guidance.

required_reviewer_teams.description: Teams whose members are permitted to review and resolve knowledge conflicts in this domain. A reviewer satisfies the requirement when their 'team' field matches any entry here. Empty array (or field omitted) = any team member may review.

Thresholds.title: Global Thresholds
Thresholds.description: Global governance thresholds used when no domain-level override is set.

conflict_threshold.description: Global semantic similarity threshold for conflict detection (0–1). Two knowledge nodes above this threshold are flagged as potentially conflicting and sent to the review queue. Start at 0.85 and tune once you have real data — higher values = fewer (but higher-confidence) conflicts.

authority_threshold.description: Authority delta above which a conflict is auto-resolved in favour of the higher-authority author (0–1). When |authority_A - authority_B| > this value, Quorum resolves automatically without human review. Start at 0.20 — lower values auto-resolve more aggressively; higher values send more conflicts to humans.

Notifications.title: Notification Config
Notifications.description: Webhook notification settings (GAP-17). Quorum fires a POST to webhook_url whenever a conflict enters the human review queue.

webhook_url.description: HTTP(S) URL to POST when a conflict.pending_review event fires. Quorum sends a JSON payload: { event, project_id, conflict_id, dashboard_url, actors, summary }. Wire this to a Slack incoming webhook, email relay, or PagerDuty Events API endpoint.

dashboard_url.description: Override for the dashboard base URL used to build the deep-link in the webhook payload. Defaults to QUORUM_DASHBOARD_URL env var. Set this if your team accesses the dashboard at a non-default URL.
